Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Test case intent: In PosixParserTest.setUp(), the defined short options are: a (no arg), b (requires arg), c (no arg). The failing test testStopBursting() parses args ["-azc"] with stopAtNonOption=true and expects exactly one extra (non-option) argument. The desired outcome is: option -a, and a single non-option argument "zc".
- Reported symptom: The issue summary describes that when stopAtNonOption is enabled, bursting continues even after encountering a non-option character, leading to options being parsed beyond the first non-option. Example given: "-azb" becomes "-a zb -b" instead of "-a zb".
- Parsing flow in code:
  - org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.flatten(Options, String[], boolean) (lines 97–164) iterates over tokens. For multi-char tokens starting with '-', if not a full long/short option, it calls burstToken(token, stopAtNonOption) (lines 130–146).
  - org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.burstToken(String, boolean) (lines 282–310) iterates characters of the token from index 1:
    - If the char is a known option (options.hasOption(ch)), it adds "-<ch>" to tokens (lines 288–292). If that option takes an argument and there are remaining chars, it adds the remainder as an argument and breaks (lines 293–298).
    - Else if stopAtNonOption is true, it calls process(token.substring(i)) (lines 300–303).
    - Else it adds the whole token and breaks (lines 304–308).
  - org.apache.commons.cli.PosixParser.process(String) (lines 197–217) when not expecting an argument for the current option, sets eatTheRest=true and pushes the special "--" token followed by the value (lines 213–216), signaling the end of options.
- What happens with "-azc":
  1. In burstToken:
     - i=1: 'a' is an option, so tokens add "-a". currentOption set to 'a' (no arg). Loop continues.
     - i=2: 'z' is not an option and stopAtNonOption is true, so process("zc") is called. In process, since currentOption ('a') does not take an argument, it sets eatTheRest=true and adds "--" and "zc" to tokens.
  2. Bug: After calling process("zc"), burstToken does not stop. There is no break after process(...). The loop continues with i=3:
     - i=3: 'c' is a valid option; burstToken adds "-c" to tokens (line 290).
  3. The resulting token stream becomes ["-a", "--", "zc", "-c"].
  4. Because "--" indicates end-of-options, the parser will treat everything after it as non-option arguments. Therefore, both "zc" and "-c" are counted as extra args, making cl.getArgList().size() == 2 instead of the expected 1.
- Root cause: In burstToken(String, boolean), when stopAtNonOption is true and a non-option character is encountered (line 300), the method calls process(remainder) but fails to break out of the loop. This allows subsequent characters to be erroneously burst into options, even though stopAtNonOption logic should have halted bursting and treated the remainder as a single non-option argument.
- Expected fix: Ensure burstToken stops bursting after encountering the first non-option character when stopAtNonOption is true (e.g., add a break immediately after process(token.substring(i))). This will yield tokens ["-a", "--", "zc"], producing exactly one extra arg and satisfying the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
